header.name: Concepts and Methods in Social Movement Research
header.description: The course provides a crisp and in-depth review of the conceptual history of social movements research. Beginning with the mid 20th Century, it shows how contentious politics emerged as a major field of study and theories of new social movements (NSM) offered a conceptual and empirical basis for it. The course offers students a critique of the NSM and its limitations in terms of the paradox of ‘unmediated’ collective action. Further, it takes up themes of charisma, ideology and opportunity structures including the relationship between global North and South and discusses the methodological challenges for movement studies. Finally, the course discusses alternative approaches used in studies of movements in the 21st Century and the conceptual and methdological innovations that accompany the same.
prerequisites_mandatory: Introduction level course in any of the major social sciences including critical thihking
prerequisites_desirable: Introduction to Sociology/New Media and Politics

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to recall key concepts and their empirical basis from the early theory of NSM

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Having understood key concepts, students then discuss the limitations of NSM in light of the changes brought about by political, technological and ecologic change since the 1980s

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Having considered the limits of NSM, students then apply these to explain the paradox of 'unmediated' politics and persistence of charsima and mediation in social movement research

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can showcase their grasp of concepts through developing independent case studies and demonstrate the various innovations in methods to study to social movements in 21st C

lecture_topics: NSM theories and social movements research
Methods and the future of movement studies
